about: Where each color in utils/colors.py comes from. A string is a name in rnv-brand (TABLE.key, or one of its own constants, in engine/brand.py); an object is a value this application owns, with the reason. Edit this file, then run: python tools/sync_colors.py

GRAY_44.why: gray(4) on the register's ink grid, which the register states as a rule and does not name.

GRAY_55.why: gray(5) on the register's ink grid, which the register states as a rule and does not name.

GRAY_66.why: gray(6) on the register's ink grid, which the register states as a rule and does not name.

GRAY_88.why: gray(8) on the register's ink grid, which the register states as a rule and does not name.

GRAY_CC.why: gray(12) on the register's ink grid, which the register states as a rule and does not name.

GRAY_DD.why: gray(13) on the ramp. Edges and lines that share APP text's hex without being ink.

GRAY_E0.why: gray(14) on the ramp. Static light surfaces that share pressed-light's hex without being a pressed state.

GRAY_EE.why: gray(14) on the ramp. Static light surfaces, such as the diff headers, that share hover-light's hex without being a hover.

SEMANTIC_DIFF_ADDED.why: The diff view's added line, in dark.

SEMANTIC_DIFF_REMOVED.why: The diff view's removed line, in dark.

SEMANTIC_DIFF_CHANGED.why: The diff view's changed line, in dark.

SEMANTIC_DIFF_ADDED_LIGHT.why: The diff view's added line, in light.

SEMANTIC_DIFF_REMOVED_LIGHT.why: The diff view's removed line, in light.

SEMANTIC_DIFF_CHANGED_LIGHT.why: The diff view's changed line, in light.

SEMANTIC_REGEX_MATCH.why: A regular expression's match, highlighted, in dark.

SEMANTIC_REGEX_MATCH_LIGHT.why: A regular expression's match, highlighted, in light.

SEMANTIC_EXPORT_FOOTER.why: Data: the 'Generated by' footer of an exported PDF or RTF, and an exported RTF's line numbers.

SEMANTIC_EXPORT_RTF_INK.why: Data, not chrome: the RTF export's text color. It does not follow the brand's black (#48 A).

SEMANTIC_HEX_PATTERN_EXAMPLE.why: Data: the example the Hex Color regex pattern carries, in the upper case it is written in (#56 A).
